title: Poem VI
text:
She lived-she could live-with a word clenched between her lips.

She died with the word clenched between her lips.

They threw earth over the word.

The lips came undone beneath the earth.

And still the clenched word remained, I do not know where!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the word physically clenched beyond lips, burial, and decay.

title: If You Love Me, Love Me Whole...
text:
If you love me, love me whole,

not by zones of light or shadow...

if you love me, love me black

and white. And gray, and green, and blond,

love me day,

love me night...

And dawn at the open window!


If you love me, do not cut me down:

love all of me... or do not love me!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Loynaz's demand to be loved without dividing or trimming the self.

title: Love Me Whole
text:
If you love me, love me whole,

not by zones of light or shadow...

If you love me, love me black

and white. And gray, and green, and blond,

and brunette...

Love me day,

love me night...

And dawn at the open window!


If you love me, do not cut me down:

Love all of me... Or do not love me!
editorial_note: The translation preserves this variant's added 'brunette' line and capitalized final command.

title: I Cast My Hope into the Sea...
text:
I cast my hope into the sea:


and even in the sea, my hope was


                                      sea-green...


 I cast my song into the sea:


and even in the sea, my song was


                                    crystal...


 Then I cast your love into the sea...


and even in the sea your love was


                                     salt...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the spaced visual endings: sea-green, crystal, and salt.

title: This Girl Is Painted...
text:
This girl is painted

on rice paper that is transparent

to the light; she flies in her paper

through the air... She flies with the dry leaves

and with lost sighs.

She is the girl of paper and flight;

she is the light, the weightless

girl of illuminated paper,

the one with watercolors...

The one no one would dare

to kiss for fear of erasing her...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the fragile watercolor girl as something loved too delicately to touch.
